newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FOURTH AUSTRALIAN ATHLETE DIES IN ISRAEL.
newsitem.headline: FOURTH AUSTRALIAN ATHLETE DIES IN ISRAEL.

text.p: A fourth Australian injured in a bridge collapse at Israel's "Jewish Olympics" last month died on Sunday in Tel Aviv, hospital officials said.

Warren Zienes, 56 of Sydney, died after contracting an infection when he fell into the marshy Yarkon River as he and teammates walked over a bridge toward the stadium for the opening ceremony of the 51-nation Maccabiah games.
Dirty water caused the infection, a hospital spokeswoman said. "He came in here in very bad condition," she said.
The wooden bridge buckled as competitors from the 370-member Australian team were walking across it on July 14.
An Israeli inquiry found last month that faulty design, materials and construction led to the disaster.
The seven-member committee submitted its findings to the government but refrained from recommending any criminal indictments pending completion of a police investigation.

Two Australians from Sydney -- ten-pin bowler Greg Small, 37, and 50-year-old Yetty Bennet, section manager of the men's bowling team -- died when the bridge collapsed and 43 other athletes were injured.
Twelve days later, 47-year-old Elizabeth Sawicki of Melbourne died of lung damage caused by poisons in the water.
A spokesman for the Australian contingent has demanded that Israel compensate the surviving victims and the families of the dead.
